finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: the POST 'feed' parameter is passed unvalidated to file_get_contents(), letting any remote client make the server fetch arbitrary URLs (and file:// or php:// wrappers when enabled).
finding.source: import.php:11 - $_POST['feed'], supplied by any unauthenticated HTTP client; only REQUEST_METHOD==='POST' and isset() are checked.

trace.note: Guard is only method and isset check; attacker satisfies both.
Attacker-controlled URL reaches file_get_contents with no transformation.
Response returns only strlen of fetched body, giving a length oracle rather than full-response SSRF.

finding.guards_checked: No require_admin on this branch; no scheme or host allowlist; no private/loopback/link-local IP blocking; no redirect restriction (file_get_contents follows redirects by default); no timeout or size limit. Exploitability depends on allow_url_fopen and display_errors in php.ini, which is not in the repo.

verdict.guard_found: none. import.php:11 checks only REQUEST_METHOD === 'POST' and isset($_POST['feed']). import.php:12 passes $_POST['feed'] straight to file_get_contents() with no scheme, host, or IP allowlist. require_admin() (import.php:4-9) is called only on the set_webhook branch (line 18), not on the feed branch.
verdict.reason: The feed value at import.php:11 is set by any unauthenticated POST, and no closing guard exists before the file_get_contents() sink at import.php:12, so the server fetches an attacker-chosen URL. The trace is accurate: line 13 returns only strlen($xml), which limits the attacker to a length oracle, and exploitability of non-HTTP wrappers depends on allow_url_fopen, which is not in the repo.

finding.claim: Admin-gated blind SSRF: the POST 'set_webhook' parameter is passed unvalidated to curl_init/curl_exec, letting an admin session (or a CSRF-driven admin browser) make the server request arbitrary URLs.
finding.source: import.php:17-19 - $_POST['set_webhook'], supplied by a client holding a session where $_SESSION['is_admin'] is truthy.

trace.note: Branch entered when set_webhook is set.
require_admin() (defined lines 4-9) only checks empty($_SESSION['is_admin']) and returns 403 if empty.
curl_exec sends the request; RETURNTRANSFER discards the response.
Prints 'ok'; no response data returned, so blind SSRF.

finding.guards_checked: require_admin session-presence check only (not role or CSRF). No URL scheme, host, or IP validation. No CSRF token on the POST; SameSite cookie behaviour not in repo. is_admin is never set in this file; correctness depends on login code outside the repo. libcurl default protocol set depends on deployed version.

verdict.guard_found: No URL scheme/host/IP validation before the sink. The only gate is require_admin() (import.php:4-9, 18), which returns 403 unless $_SESSION['is_admin'] is set. That is an admin-session gate, not a closing URL guard, so it refutes the claim only through the source check.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (import.php:17-23 matches the claim), but the POST value at import.php:19 is only reachable after require_admin() at import.php:18 passes, so it is controlled by an admin-session holder, not an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker, which the source check requires. The CSRF route is unproven: the repo has no token check, but SameSite cookie behaviour is outside the repo, so it cannot be treated as a confirmed attacker path. Separately, import.php:11-12 passes an unauthenticated $_POST['feed'] straight into file_get_contents(), which is a more serious issue that this candidate does not cover.
